title: Liquid Helium Climbs Out of Its Own Cup

scenes.text: Liquid helium can climb out of its own cup.
Cool helium below minus 271 degrees Celsius and it becomes a superfluid. All friction vanishes.
It coats the glass in a film about thirty nanometers thick, roughly a hundred atoms.
That film creeps up the wall, slides over the rim, and drips off the bottom.
It keeps going until the cup is completely empty.
A liquid that climbs out of its own container.
